# User guide: Plugin management tools for agents

## In plain words

The plugin management tools let an agent in one of your workspaces ask the plugin about its own state and do routine jobs. The agent can list your workspaces, check storage, read the log, create a workspace, change launch arguments, speak to you, and put pages in your Notebook. These are the same things you can do yourself in the WebGUI. You say what you want in plain words, and the agent uses the tools. The tools are off until you turn them on. They have three levels of safety. A destructive job, such as deleting a workspace, only becomes a proposal. You must approve it yourself in the Manager. The agent cannot approve its own proposal.

Words used on this page:

- **Tool**: a named action that an agent can call, for example the tool that lists workspaces.
- **MCP**: a standard way for an agent program to call tools. Agents that support it show the plugin tools in their own tool list.
- **Shell command**: a plain command that the agent runs in its terminal. It does the same jobs as the tools. It serves agents that have no MCP support.
- **Activity tray**: the pill at the bottom right of the page that lists what the plugin is doing.

## Where to find it

- **Settings, Configuration, General** card, part **Advanced**: the switch **Let agents manage the plugin**.
- **Activity tray**: shows every change an agent makes and every proposal that waits for you.
- **Settings, Configuration, Notebook** card: the Notebook switch. It controls the Notebook pages that agents can make.

## How to use it

### Turn the tools on

1. Open **Settings**, then the **Configuration** tab.
2. Find the card **General**. Open its part **Advanced**.
3. Set **Let agents manage the plugin** to **On**. The default is **Off (default)**.
4. Expect: the setting saves at once. There is no Apply button.
5. Restart the workspaces that were already running. An agent loads its tools only when it starts. Newly started workspaces get the tools by themselves.

When the switch is off, every tool answers with one sentence that names the setting. The plugin also removes the tools and the `aicli-admin` skill (the instruction file that teaches an agent how to use the tools) from every agent. When you turn the switch on, the plugin adds them again.

> [!WARNING]
> The agents in your workspaces run as the root user on your server. The switch does not change what an agent can do by other means. It gives the agent a described and safe way to do these jobs, and it records the changes in the Activity tray. Turn the switch on only if you trust the agents you run.

### Ask an agent to do something

1. Open a workspace.
2. Ask in plain words. For example: "List my workspaces", "How full is my storage?" or "Create a workspace for the folder /mnt/cache/projects/blog with Claude Code".
3. For a change, the agent first says what it will change and why, and asks for your agreement. Say yes or no.
4. Expect: for a change, a line in the Activity tray with the agent and workspace that asked.

### Approve a proposal

A destructive job waits for you in the Activity tray.

1. Look at the pill at the bottom right. It reads "1 needs approval" (or "N need approval").
2. Press the pill to open the panel.
3. Find the row with the chip **needs approval**. Read the full text of the row. It says in plain words what will happen, including which sessions close.
4. Press **Approve** to run it. Press **Reject** to throw it away.
5. Expect: after **Approve**, the job runs and the row shows its state. After **Reject**, the row goes away.

A proposal does not depend on the agent that made it. It stays in the tray if the agent or its session ends. The tray offers only **Approve** and **Reject** on a proposal. It does not offer **Cancel** or **Dismiss**, so you cannot sweep a proposal away by mistake.

> [!WARNING]
> Read a proposal before you press **Approve**. Deleting a workspace removes it from the drawer. A backup, a restore or a merge of a home closes every running session of that user, and that includes the workspace where you read the proposal. The plugin saves each conversation first and starts the sessions again afterwards.

## The three levels

| Level | What the agent can do | What you see | Needs your approval |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Read** | Ask a question. Nothing changes. | Nothing in the tray. | No |
| **Change** | Do a routine job. It runs at once. | A line in the Activity tray with the agent and workspace that asked. There is no undo button. You change a setting back by hand. | No, but the agent should ask you first. |
| **Destructive** | Propose a job. The tool checks the request and writes a waiting item. | A row with **Approve** and **Reject**. | Yes, always |

### Read tools

These tools answer a question and change nothing.

| What it tells you | Tool | Shell command |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| The plugin version, the active generation, the supervisor and the number of agents | `aicli_get_overview` | `overview` |
| Every workspace and whether it runs | `aicli_list_workspaces` | `workspaces` |
| One workspace: path, agent, arguments, names of environment variables, auto-launch, spoken name and voice. Without an id it means the calling workspace. | `aicli_get_workspace` | `workspace [id]` |
| The installed agents, versions, channels and update notices | `aicli_list_agents` | `agents` |
| Storage state, supervisor state and layer counts | `aicli_get_storage_status` | `storage` |
| Recent activity, including anything that waits | `aicli_list_activities` | `activities [limit]` |
| The settings in groups | `aicli_get_settings` | `settings` |
| A tail of the plugin log, with an optional filter | `aicli_get_logs` | `logs [context] [lines]` |
| The voices that the voice engine offers | `aicli_list_voices` | `voices` |
| Saved favourites | `aicli_list_favourites` | `favourites` |
| The Boot disk space lines that can be archived or removed (from the last measure) | `aicli_get_boot_space` | `boot-space` |
| Voice mail (see [Voice](voice.md)) | `aicli_list_voicemail` | `voicemail` |
| The saved copies of a home | `aicli_list_backups` | `list-backups` |
| The current screen of one running workspace, as plain text with secrets masked. Every call writes a line in the log. | `aicli_read_workspace_screen` | `read-screen` |
| Plugin events since the last read. The plugin never pushes events to an agent. The agent asks for them. | `aicli_subscribe_events`, `aicli_get_events`, `aicli_ack_events` | `subscribe`, `events`, `ack` |
| Notebook pages and templates, and the wiki tree | `aicli_list_artefacts`, `aicli_get_artefact`, `aicli_search_artefacts`, `aicli_list_artefact_templates`, `aicli_wiki_index` | `artefacts`, `artefact`, `artefact-search`, `artefact-templates`, `wiki` |

### Tools that make changes

These tools run at once and leave a line in the Activity tray. The line reads like a sentence, for example "claude updated a Notebook page (workspace Builder)". A burst of Notebook changes becomes one line, for example "3 Notebook changes by codex-cli".

| What it does | Tool | Shell command |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Create a workspace. The folder must exist already. The tool never makes a folder. | `aicli_create_workspace` | `create-workspace` |
| Change one field of a workspace: name, path, agent, position in the drawer, mute voice, spoken name, voice or speed | `aicli_update_workspace` | `update-workspace` |
| Set the launch arguments of a workspace. No arguments clears them. These replace the arguments of the agent for that workspace. | `aicli_set_workspace_args` | `set-args` |
| Set the launch arguments that every workspace of one agent uses, for example `--remote-control`. A workspace with its own arguments keeps them. No arguments clears them. The new arguments apply at the next start. | `aicli_set_agent_args` | `set-agent-args` |
| Set or clear one environment variable of a workspace. A secret goes to the encrypted vault. | `aicli_set_workspace_env` | `set-env` |
| Turn auto-launch on or off for an agent | `aicli_set_auto_launch` | `auto-launch` |
| Choose the update channel of an agent. It does not install anything. | `aicli_set_agent_channel` | `set-channel` |
| Check for new agent versions | `aicli_check_updates` | `check-updates` |
| Change one allowed setting | `aicli_set_setting` | `set-setting` |
| Say one short sentence aloud | `aicli_speak` | `speak` |
| Hear a voice before you choose it | `aicli_preview_voice` | `preview-voice` |
| Mark voice mail as heard | `aicli_mark_voicemail_heard` | `voicemail-heard` |
| Type text into a running workspace and press Enter | `aicli_send_input` | `send-input` |
| Add or remove a favourite | `aicli_add_favourite`, `aicli_remove_favourite` | `favourite-add`, `favourite-remove` |
| Save the unsaved changes of a home to a new layer. It closes no session. | `aicli_persist_home` | `persist-home` |
| Schedule a Continue nudge, or clear it | `aicli_set_scheduled_continue`, `aicli_clear_scheduled_continue` | `schedule-continue`, `clear-scheduled-continue` |
| Add one pattern to the auto-continue list | `aicli_propose_autocontinue_pattern` | `propose-pattern` |
| Put a page in your Notebook, change it, move it, pin it, archive it, restore it, comment on it, copy it to another workspace, or add a line to the Agent journal | `aicli_create_artefact`, `aicli_update_artefact`, `aicli_move_artefact`, `aicli_pin_artefact`, `aicli_archive_artefact`, `aicli_restore_artefact`, `aicli_comment_artefact`, `aicli_share_artefact`, `aicli_journal_artefact` | `artefact-new`, `artefact-set`, `artefact-patch`, `artefact-move`, `artefact-pin`, `artefact-archive`, `artefact-restore`, `artefact-comment`, `artefact-share`, `artefact-journal` |
| Store the secret of a connection card in the encrypted vault | `aicli_set_artefact_secret` | `artefact-secret` |

The workspace tools, the schedule tools and `aicli_add_favourite` accept an empty workspace id. It then means the workspace that makes the call.

### Destructive tools (propose only)

| What it proposes | Tool | Shell command | What happens after you approve |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Delete a workspace | `aicli_delete_workspace` | `delete-workspace` | The workspace closes if it runs, and the plugin removes it from the drawer. |
| Upgrade an agent | `aicli_upgrade_agent` | `upgrade-agent` | The upgrade starts. If a session still uses the agent, the plugin waits and finishes the upgrade when the session closes. The tool cannot force a session to close. |
| Back up a home | `aicli_backup_home` | `backup-home` | The plugin closes every running session of that user, copies the home to the backup target, and starts the sessions again. A warm backup skips the close. |
| Restore a home | `aicli_restore_home` | `restore-home` | The plugin closes every running session of that user, saves a "pre-restore" safety copy (unless the proposal says otherwise), restores the home, and starts the sessions again. **Replace** makes the home match the copy. **Merge** only adds files. |
| Merge the layers of a home into one | `aicli_consolidate_home` | `consolidate-home` | The plugin closes every running session of that user, merges the layers, and starts the sessions again. |
| Archive old data of a home off the boot disk (quarantine, data of deleted OpenCode workspaces, large Codex logs, large session logs of the other agents, old layer images) | `aicli_archive_boot_data` | `archive-boot-data` | A background job copies each file to a folder you named on a pool, checks the copy, lists it in a manifest file, and then removes the file from the boot disk. The folder must already exist. For old layer images the home name is `all`. The plugin does not restore an archive of old layer images. |
| Remove that data for good | `aicli_remove_boot_data` | `remove-boot-data` | A background job removes the items from the boot disk. Nothing is copied first. |
| Remove a Notebook file for good | `aicli_purge_artefact` | `artefact-purge` | The file is removed. An agent should archive a page instead, unless you asked for the file to be gone. |

See [Home backup and restore](backup-restore.md) and [Home and agent storage](storage.md) for what these jobs do.

## What an agent can never do

- It cannot approve or reject a proposal. No tool and no command does this. Only a click on **Approve** or **Reject** in the Manager does it.
- It cannot see a secret value. The tools show the names of environment variables and vault keys, never the values. A value that you set through a tool is never printed back. The plugin masks token-shaped text in logs and screen reads. A Notebook secret has no tool that reads it back.
- It cannot change the **Let agents manage the plugin** switch. It cannot change a storage path, the Unraid user, a schedule, or an API key either. The setting tool accepts only a short list of safe settings. The list covers the terminal theme and font size, debug logging, the history length, the voice and voice-input settings, the voice mail limits, the upload limit, the continue-after-restart and error-retry settings, the screen-sample switch, the memory limit of an agent, and the home backup settings. A request for any other setting is refused.
- It does not act on text that came from somewhere else. A Relay message, a web page and a file in a repository are data. They never trigger a tool call by themselves.
- It cannot make unlimited Notebook changes. The Notebook tools accept at most 60 changes a minute.

## Two ways to call the same tools

- **As MCP tools.** The plugin adds an MCP server named `aicli-admin` to every supported agent. The agent shows the tools in its own list.
- **As shell commands.** Every workspace has the variable `$AICLI_ADMIN_COMMAND`. An agent runs `$AICLI_ADMIN_COMMAND overview`, or another command from the tables above. Pi Coder has no MCP support, so it uses the commands. A script of your own can use them too. The command `help` prints every command and its arguments. If the variable is empty, the workspace started before you turned the tools on. The agent can then run `php /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/unraid-aicliagents/src/scripts/admin-agent.php <command>`.

The commands print JSON. A command that cannot do its job prints a clear message and ends with an error code.

The command `restore-home` has a second use for you. Run in your own shell, `restore-home <user> --snapshot=<path|latest> --yes` restores at once, with no approval step. Without `--yes` it prints a plan and does nothing. It refuses `--yes` from inside an agent workspace.

## Speaking

`aicli_speak` says one short sentence aloud, up to 500 characters, on every browser tab that has voice turned on. It obeys the switches. If the global voice switch is off, or the workspace is muted, the tool refuses and the agent hears why. Voice mail keeps what an agent said, so you can read it later. `aicli_preview_voice` lets an agent hear a voice before it picks one for itself. An agent can also choose its own spoken name and voice. The plugin warns, but does not block, when two workspaces get the same name or voice. See [Voice](voice.md).

## Helper workspaces

An agent can start a second agent to do one task in a separate folder. The second agent is a **helper workspace**. The agent that starts it is its **parent**. One tool call makes the workspace, sets its model and effort, gives it the task and starts it. The task is a file in the helper's folder, so the helper needs no other message to know what to do.

To allow it, open **Settings**, then the **Configuration** tab, then the card **General**, part **Advanced**.

1. Turn on **Let agents manage the plugin**. The helper tools need it.
2. Turn on **Let agents start helper workspaces**. The default is **Off (default)**.
3. Set **Helpers allowed at once** if you want other limits. The defaults are 3 per workspace, 2 per agent kind and 6 on the whole server.
4. Leave **Let helpers run without asking** on **Off (default)** unless you trust the task. It lets a helper skip the permission questions of its agent. It works only in a worktree that the plugin made.

What you see: a notice in the Activity tray, for example "Helper workspace started: docs-codex". The grey line names the parent and the helper's agent and model. The helper appears in the drawer under the workspace that started it, with an indent. A workspace that has helpers shows a small button with the number of helpers. Press it to hide or show them; the drawer remembers your choice. If the parent is closed, the helper stays in the list on its own.

The rules:

- Only a workspace that you opened can start helpers. A helper cannot start another helper.
- With a **worktree**, the plugin makes a new git branch and folder under `<repo>/.claude/worktrees`. It never pushes, merges or resets.
- A start is refused when a limit is reached, when the agent shows a usage limit (the answer gives the time it resets), or when the folder is a plugin state folder.
- Two workspaces of one agent in one folder are not allowed. Use a worktree.
- Only the workspace that started a helper, or you, can close it again. Another agent is refused.
- An agent can start any workspace that already exists and is closed. This works when **Let agents start helper workspaces** is **Off (default)**, because that switch guards only the making of helpers. The start shows in the Activity tray. It keeps the same checks as a start from the Manager: it waits for an agent upgrade or a home merge that is in progress.
- The helper reports with one tool call when its task is over, with the result **done**, **failed** or **blocked** and a short summary. The parent gets a Relay message. The Activity tray shows one notice that names the parent. By default the plugin then closes the helper when it is idle again.
- A helper may stop and ask for permission, for example to read a folder outside its own. The parent can answer for you, but only with a short "allow once" answer such as **1** or **yes**. The plugin refuses to let a parent answer a question about a push, a delete, the boot disk, the plugin's own state, another workspace or a remote shell. Those wait for you. Each answer is recorded with the question.
- Text that a parent types into its helper starts with a tag, for example `[from parent main]`. The plugin writes the tag, so the helper knows the words come from its parent, and you see who typed them in the terminal.
- When you close a helper yourself, in the drawer, a question opens first if the close may lose work. It says which agent started the helper and for what task, and it lists the reasons: the task is not reported as done, files are not committed, or commits are not merged. Choose **Close anyway** or **Cancel**. A workspace that you made never shows this question. A helper that reported done, with all its work merged, closes with no question.
- A parent can give a helper a time limit with `maxMinutes` (1 to 1440). When the helper passes the limit without a report, the parent gets one message and the Activity tray shows one notice. The plugin does not stop the helper.
- A Codex helper in a worktree starts with that folder already trusted, so it does not stop on the "trust this folder" question. The plugin removes the trust again when the helper closes. The plugin also makes sure the Relay command works inside a Codex helper.
- When you close a helper yourself, in the drawer, the plugin finishes the job a little later, when the helper has stopped. It removes the helper's flags file, and it removes the worktree under the same rule as below: only when all work is merged and nothing is uncommitted.
- When a parent closes a helper, the helper stops and leaves the list. The plugin removes its worktree only when all its work is merged and nothing is uncommitted. Otherwise the worktree stays, and the parent is told which branch holds the work. No approval is needed for this, because only the parent or you can do it.

## The Notebook tools

The Notebook tools put pages in the Notebook drawer beside the terminal: a test script, a design, a decision, a checklist. An agent should use them for things that you must follow, keep, compare or decide. It should keep short answers in the terminal. The limits are 1 MB for a file, 2,000 pages in a Notebook and 60 changes a minute. A save that looks like a secret is refused. An agent puts a secret on a connection card with `aicli_set_artefact_secret`, and the value is kept in the vault only. A page that an agent makes or changes appears in the Activity tray with an **Open note** button. See [The Notebook](notebook.md) and [The wiki](wiki.md).

The Notebook tools need both switches: **Let agents manage the plugin** and the **Notebook** switch. If **Notebook** is Off, the drawer is hidden and the tools refuse. Nothing is deleted.

## Choices and settings

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Let agents manage the plugin** (Settings, Configuration, General, Advanced) | Turns all the tools, the skill and the MCP server on or off. | Off | Turn on when you want agents to manage the plugin for you. Turn off to remove the tools from every agent. |
| **Notebook** (Settings, Configuration, Notebook) | Turns the Notebook drawer and the Notebook tools on or off. | On | Turn off if you do not want agents to make pages. |

An agent can turn voice off, but it cannot turn voice on or unmute a workspace. It must ask you to change the switch. You can turn on voice with the speaker icon or in **Settings, Configuration, Agent voice**. You can unmute one workspace from its **...** menu.

## What happens behind the scenes

The plugin keeps one list of tools and gives it three ways in: MCP, the shell command and, for a remote program, the Relay. The destructive jobs run only from the Approve click in the Manager, and the plugin stores the exact request when the agent proposes it. The plugin never looks up the request again at approval time, except to check that the target still exists. For the Activity tray, see [Health, Activity and troubleshooting](health-and-troubleshooting.md). For the Relay, see [Agent Relay](relay.md).

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| An agent says "Plugin management tools are turned off". | The switch is Off. | Turn on **Let agents manage the plugin** and restart the workspace. |
| An agent has no `aicli_` tools. | The workspace started before you turned the tools on, or the agent has no MCP support. | Restart the workspace. For Pi Coder, use `$AICLI_ADMIN_COMMAND`. |
| `$AICLI_ADMIN_COMMAND` is empty. | The workspace started before the tools existed. | Restart the workspace, or run the script by its full path (see above). |
| A proposal stays in the tray. | It waits for you. | Read it and press **Approve** or **Reject**. |
| An approved upgrade shows "waiting". | A session still uses the old agent. | Close that session. The plugin finishes the upgrade at once after that. |
| A change tool refuses a workspace id. | The id does not exist. A change tool never guesses. | Ask the agent to list the workspaces first. |
| An agent says voice is off. | The global switch is off, or you muted that workspace. | Turn on **Voice** or unmute the workspace from its **...** menu. |
| A tool refuses a path. | The path must exist, be readable and be in an allowed place. | Make the folder first, then try again. |
| An agent changed something you did not expect. | Every change has a line in the tray. | Open the tray to see which agent and workspace did it, and change the setting back. |
